title: Per‑token SLA sentinels, incremental trace anchors, and escaped‑output scrubber for streamed tool calls
creator: Lena Park
description:
Problem: Current streaming telemetry bundles per-request aggregates which hides short-lived SLA violations during long tool/function calls and interleaved structured outputs. Traces can lose alignment with the incremental tokens emitted by the model when function/tool responses are streamed in pieces. Additionally, downstream logs occasionally capture partially emitted structured output (escaped sequences, JSON fragments) which complicates redaction and raises PII leakage risk.

Goal: Add lightweight per-token/per-chunk SLA sentinels and incremental trace anchors so we can: 1) detect and alert on transient token-latency spikes, 2) correlate partial tool-call outputs with spans deterministically, and 3) run an escaped-output scrubber that prevents logging of incomplete structured fragments while preserving observability metadata.

Scope: engineering team implementation for hosted API runtime and Redwood Console ingestion path. Does not include Dedicated autoscaler changes; compatibility layer support (legacy SDKs) included as opt-in headers.

Technical approach:
- Instrumentation: emit a minimal sentinel event every N tokens (configurable, default 16) with fields: sentinel_id (UUID4), token_index, elapsed_since_last_sentinel_ms, active_tool_call_id (if any). Sentinels are lightweight and encoded as span events so they attach to the active trace.
- Incremental trace anchors: create deterministic anchor spans at sentinel boundaries that contain a short stable fingerprint (sha1 of prefix window) to allow reassembly across retries/fanout. Anchors are sampled at a lower rate for high-volume customers.
- Escaped-output scrubber: before any streamed chunk is emitted to logs or long-term telemetry, run a stateful scrubber that recognizes open structured tokens (unclosed JSON/object/array or incomplete escape sequences) and either buffer until closure or redact the fragment while emitting a placeholder token and a scrubber-hash for debugging. The scrubber will use configurable policies: block-then-wait (buffer up to M bytes), redact-partial, redact-all.
- Tool/function calling alignment: when the runtime starts a tool call, it tags the current sentinel stream with a tool_call_id and fanout_id; all subsequent sentinels include that id so tool output can be correlated even if tool response arrives interleaved or via fallback.
- Compatibility headers: legacy SDKs can opt into "X-RW-Sentinel: disabled"; default behavior is enabled. Add guidance in SDK changelogs.

Acceptance criteria (must be testable):
- Sentinel events appear in traces and are queryable in Console for a synthetic workload.
- At least one alert rule demonstrates detection of transient token-latency > 250ms for 3 consecutive sentinels.
- Tool calls in integration tests produce a consistent tool_call_id across streamed fragments and corresponding spans link to the same anchor.
- Escaped-output scrubber prevents incomplete JSON fragments from appearing in logs in >99.99% of runs for test corpus (see attachments).
- Backwards compatibility: legacy SDK with header disabled sees no sentinel events in traces.

Rollout plan: feature flagged A/B rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with metrics gated on CPU overhead (<3% p95 increase) and telemetry throughput (<5% increase). Canary in hosted, then opt-in for Dedicated via config. Console will add a Sentinels tab in streaming traces UI.

Instrumentation cost & perf considerations: sentinels are compact (approx 64-128 bytes) and grouped when possible. Sampling for anchors reduces cardinality. Escaped-output scrubber runs in-line but bounded buffer sizes to avoid backpressure; worst-case behavior is to redact (fail-open) to maintain latency SLOs.

Privacy & security: scrubber rules will be reviewed by privacy and security teams. We will not persist raw incomplete fragments; only scrubber-hash and sentinel metadata are stored.

Docs & SDKs: add telemetry section to runtime-1.22 release notes and SDK migration guide showing header, tuning knobs, and examples for function calls.
